what_it_does: Universities that own GPU clusters (racks of graphics processing units — the chips used to train AI models) face a different operating environment from large tech companies: they have small IT staffs, a mix of old and new hardware from different eras, and many researchers with different needs all competing for the same machines. Existing cluster management software is built for industrial-scale deployments and does not translate well to this setting. SING is a four-layer management system designed specifically for campus GPU clusters, covering automated hardware setup and health monitoring, fair scheduling of jobs across users (so no single lab can monopolize the cluster), a user-friendly job submission interface, and automated detection and logging of hardware failures. The design goal is to keep the cluster running with minimal manual intervention from a small team.
